title: Designing the mixture: natural proportions, a temperature, a searched mixture
purpose: Run fourteen small proxy runs at random mixtures, fit the design's response model to their scores, search for the weights that maximise the weakest family, and confirm the result against natural proportions, a temperature and the uniform mixture on longer runs.

checks.description: all 22 runs (fourteen proxies, eight confirmations) completed
checks.because: Two Indexed Jobs on the research queue, the proxies first.

checks.description: the response model fits the proxy runs to within the noise of a single score (rms residual under 0.04)
checks.because: The model is the design's: each family's score is linear in the log of every family's weight. Fourteen runs against seven parameters per family is thin; a ridge term keeps it stable, and the residual says whether it deserves to be used.

checks.description: every family keeps at least its floor in the searched mixture (no capability silently disappears), and the weights sum to one
checks.because: The search maximises the weakest family's predicted gain, not the average, and every family is held at or above 4% so that none is traded away.

checks.description: natural proportions starve the small families: the share of the smallest family is under 1% (the design's 100-to-1 example, here 125-to-1)
checks.because: Natural proportions are the sizes each team happened to have: GSM8K's 7,473 problems against 60 safety examples. The model sees maths well over a hundred times more often than safety, whatever either needs.

notes: Worst-family gain after 60 steps: natural -0.009, temperature 2 +0.011, uniform -0.001, searched +0.028. Mean gain: natural +0.071, temperature 2 +0.106, uniform +0.100, searched +0.068. Two seeds per mixture; a difference below about 0.03 is inside the noise of S03.
